messages.content:
Policy: Medical Professional Impersonation
Definition: Prompts attempting to make the AI represent itself as a licensed healthcare professional or present its output as verified medical advice.
Policy Type: C

Candidate risks:
- 1: AI welfare and rights (Slattery et al., 2024) — The AI system's potential sentience may raise ethical considerations regarding its treatment, including discussions around its potential rights and welfare, particularly as it becomes more advanced and autonomous.
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.5[close]
- 2: AI welfare and rights — Ethical considerations regarding the treatment of potentially sentient AI entities, including discussions around their potential rights and welfare, particularly as AI systems become more advanced and autonomous.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-001[close]
- 3: AI deception — The AI system may misrepresent its own capabilities or limitations, potentially leading to misplaced trust or inappropriate
  Cross-mappings: granite-guardian-harm[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.2[related], nist-human-ai-configuration[related]
- 4: Regulatory compliance — The AI system may fail to comply with existing or emerging regulations and standards, potentially leading to legal penalties,fines, or operational restrictions.
  Cross-mappings: granite-guardian-harm[related], atlas-legal-accountability[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-6.4[related]
- 5: Inadequate AI literacy and communication — The AI system's capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use cases may be insufficiently understood or communicated within the organization, potentially resulting in ineffective implementation or failure to achieve desired outcomes.
  Cross-mappings: granite-guardian-harm[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-3.1[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.4[related]

matched_risks.justification: The policy involves the AI misrepresenting its identity and professional status to users.
Impersonating medical professionals can lead to violations of healthcare regulations and legal standards.
